meaning: The export script does not hardcode fit bounds: it parses FIT_LO/FIT_HI out of fit.jl and marks a parameter "pinned at its bound" with the same 0.98 ratio test fit.jl:1004 uses. The intent is that widening the box in fit.jl cannot leave the table asserting a stale flag.

could_move.what: The 0.98 ratio threshold is the one number not parsed from fit.jl. If fit.jl:1004 changes its ratio, the pinned flags silently disagree with the fitter.
The parse depends on fit.jl's layout for FIT_LO/FIT_HI. A rename or reformat there could make the parse fail or return wrong bounds, changing every pinned mark in the table.
Ca_v has no FIT_LO/FIT_HI and is flagged by a separate rule, so its flag is not comparable to the six stage-A rows.
The table mixes fits from different dates (081 from 2026-08-18, three re-run 2026-09-05). Flags are computed against today's bounds, not the bounds each fit ran under.

expectation: No effect on any solve or fitted value. It only changes the pinned-at-bound column and the printed ranges in the exported table. Size unknown from the context; it depends on how close the stored estimates sit to the current bounds.

check.why: Re-runs only the export, re-parsing FIT_LO/FIT_HI from fit.jl, so it shows whether the parse still works and which parameters come out pinned, without re-fitting. The reach trace found no references, so nothing else exercises this path; inspect what the script writes before running it.
